newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK November PPI data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK November PPI data.

text.p: Following is a selection of economists' reactions to UK data showing November input prices down 3.2 percent m/m and down 5.5 percent y/y, while output prices were unchanged m/m and up 2.1 percent y/y:
"Extraordinarily good, extremely surprising. The bias was for a small fall in input prices but 3.2 percent on the month is way outside the range of expectations."

"It is an erratic number, but this was erratic outside the range of expectations, so the market is going to take it extremely favourably. It does bode well for output prices on a three, four-month time horizon."

"Short sterling has ticked higher as a result and in the short term it's a very positive number -- a somewhat bigger fall than expected and the output prices also look good. But underlying output prices up 0.3 percent is perhaps a shade worse than expected. On the input prices, historically they have in practice a pretty poor predictive record for retail price inflation. So yes, a very good number, but it doesn't necessarily mean inflation is about to drop back down towards the government's target."

"UK PPIs are positive for inflation prospects and should be seen as increasing the likelihood that rates will be kept on hold at Wednesday's monetary meeting. Data...consistent with the the survey evidence pointing to still intense competitiveness pressures and to this end, ought to come as a relief after the disppointing October RPI. The PPIs do suggest that at this stage, inflation is largely under control. We expect the November RPIs to be well behaved and show some moderation on an annual basis."
